<BEGIN_SHACL>
@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#> .
@prefix ex: <https://example.org/shapes#> .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Ship shape – applies to every instance of nltl:ship.
# It propagates validation to passengers and crew members attached
# via the explicit object properties defined in the supplied ontology.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:ShipShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:targetClass nltl:ship ;
    # Each ship must have passengers that satisfy the passenger‑instruction shape
    sh:property [
        sh:path nltl:hasPassenger ;
        sh:node ex:PassengerInstructionShape ;
    ] ;
    # Each ship must have crew members that satisfy the crew‑training shape
    sh:property [
        sh:path nltl:hasCrewMemberInventory ;
        sh:node ex:CrewTrainingShape ;
    ] .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Passenger‑instruction shape – validates passenger instances linked from a ship.
# The requirement states that passengers shall be instructed in the use of
# personal survival equipment and the emergency action.  This is captured
# by the boolean property nltl:personalSurvivalEquipmentInstructionCompleted
# which must be true for each passenger.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:PassengerInstructionShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    # No targetClass – validation is triggered only via ex:ShipShape
    sh:property [
        sh:path nltl:personalSurvivalEquipmentInstructionCompleted ;
        sh:datatype xsd:boolean ;
        sh:hasValue true ;
        sh:message "Each passenger must have completed instruction in personal survival equipment (value true)." ;
    ] .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Crew‑training shape – validates crew‑member instances linked from a ship.
# The requirement states that crew shall be trained in the use of personal
# and group survival equipment.  This is represented by the boolean property
# nltl:personalAndGroupSurvivalEquipmentTrainingCompleted which must be true
# for each crew member.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:CrewTrainingShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    # No targetClass – validation is triggered only via ex:ShipShape
    sh:property [
        sh:path nltl:personalAndGroupSurvivalEquipmentTrainingCompleted ;
        sh:datatype xsd:boolean ;
        sh:hasValue true ;
        sh:message "Each crew member must have completed training for personal and group survival equipment (value true)." ;
    ] .

# NOTE: The boolean properties nltl:instructionStatus,
# nltl:crewSurvivalEquipmentTrainingStatus,
# nltl:passengerInstructionStatus,
# and nltl:personalAndGroupSurvivalEquipmentTrainingStatus have
# domain nltl:benchmarkEntity in the supplied ontology, and no explicit
# ownership binding to passenger or crewMember is provided.  They are not
# used in the activated shapes to avoid inventing ownership relationships
# that are not present in the source data.
<END_SHACL>

Those are other target classes beyond declared population (only ship). The requirement is to bound activation to supplied population boundary. We need to keep obligations but avoid using extra target classes; instead they should be used via sh:node constraints within ShipShape only. The shape should not have separate targetClass for passenger/crewMember; should use sh:path nltl:hasPassenger with node ex:PassengerInstructionShape (still defined but not targetClass). The separate shape can keep targetClass maybe removed? The SHACL spec: targetClass creates validation on instances of that class. That violates admission.

Thus modify PassengerInstructionShape and CrewTrainingShape to be node shapes (no targetClass). Keep them.

So new SHACL: same prefixes, ShipShape same. PassengerInstructionShape: a sh:NodeShape ; (no targetClass). Similarly CrewTrainingShape. Also ensure any other shapes not target extra classes.

Return within <BEGIN_SHACL> ... <END_SHACL>.
